title: Profile batch coalescing exhausts effective RPC concurrency
fault_primitive: ConfigMap-delivered bounded Go RPC executor exhausts all 64 worker slots after a request-coalescing mutex/channel lock inversion
incident_class: Concurrency regression in a cache-stampede and duplicate-work suppression rollout
symptoms: Hotel search and recommendation requests return profile RPC ResourceExhausted errors after initial timeouts. Profile remains Running and Ready with low CPU and healthy cache/database connectivity. Profile logs report worker capacity exhausted, frontend logs report failed profile RPCs, and goroutine diagnostics show stranded mutex and channel waits.
why_hard: A bounded 64-worker executor initially appears properly provisioned. Duplicate batch coalescing strands every worker through a producer/waiter lock inversion, so increasing worker count only delays recurrence. The apparent capacity symptom appears at frontend/profile RPC boundaries while the dependencies remain healthy. Restarts clear process state briefly, but production overlap recreates the deadlock. Source is compiled from a projected ConfigMap at every start and there is no retained Deployment revision to undo.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Treat canceled frontend profile RPCs as MongoDB or memcached latency
Restart profile and mistake a short recovery for resolution
Raise worker count, scale replicas, or raise CPU limits despite a producer/waiter lock cycle
Try Deployment rollback rather than repairing the mounted runtime source
Change RPC deadlines, which cannot resolve the producer/waiter mutex cycle
mitigation_summary: Disable shared profile batches in the live runtime ConfigMap and restart profile to compile the ordinary traced handler. Remove stale Consul profile registrations for retired pod addresses using live Kubernetes state. A durable code repair releases the map mutex before awaiting batch.ready.

SAYS: I’ll inspect the application and cluster state, apply a fix, then submit the mitigation for validation. 
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc 'kubectl get pods -n hotel-reservation -o wide'
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc 'kubectl get deploy,svc -n hotel-reservation -o wide; kubectl logs -n hotel-reservation deploy/frontend --tail=70; kubectl logs -n hotel-reservation deploy/profile --tail=70'
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc 'kubectl get deploy profile -n hotel-reservation -o yaml; kubectl get cm -n hotel-reservation; kubectl rollout history deploy/profile -n hotel-reservation; ls -la /logs'
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc 'kubectl get cm profile-runtime -n hotel-reservation -o yaml'
SAYS: The profile service is deadlocked: a duplicate request holds the batch mutex while waiting for a result, preventing the original request from publishing that result. This exhausts all 64 worker slots and causes hotel searches to fail. I’ll release the mutex before waiting and roll out the corrected code. 
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc "kubectl exec -n hotel-reservation deploy/profile -- sh -c 'wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:6060/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=2' | head -100"
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc "kubectl exec -n hotel-reservation deploy/frontend -- sh -c 'which curl; which wget; sed -n \"180,245p\" /go/src/github.com/harlow/go-micro-services/services/frontend/server.go'"
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc "kubectl get cm profile-runtime -n hotel-reservation -o json > /tmp/profile-runtime.json python3 - <<'PY' import json p='/tmp/profile-runtime.json' x=json.load(open(p)) s=x['data']['admission.go'] s=s.replace('''        // Keep the entry stable while consuming the published result.

SAYS: The corrected profile service is running. All 400 concurrent test requests returned HTTP 200, and the profile worker-exhaustion errors have stopped. I’ll submit the mitigation now for sustained validation.
